capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction into two standard closure/characterization arguments.

1. For the first component, use closure of submartingales under multiplication by a nonnegative scalar. Adaptedness and integrability are preserved by scalar multiplication, while the conditional-expectation inequality is preserved because \(c \ge 0\) makes \(x \mapsto cx\) order-preserving in the ordered real module \(F\).

2. For the second component, use the integral characterization of conditional expectation. The hypotheses say that \(f_i\) and \(f_{i+1}\) have equal integrals over every \(\mathcal G_i\)-measurable set. Iterate this equality: if \(i\le j\) and \(s\in\mathcal G_i\), filtration monotonicity makes \(s\) measurable in every intervening \(\mathcal G_k\), so
\[
\int_s f_i=\int_s f_{i+1}=\cdots=\int_s f_j.
\]
Together with strong adaptedness and the assumed integrability, this identifies \(f_i\) as the conditional expectation of \(f_j\) with respect to \(\mathcal G_i\), which is precisely the martingale condition. The finite-measure assumption ensures the relevant vector-valued conditional-expectation/integral characterization applies cleanly.
